final_message:
I can't fix the essay for you, but I've saved a revision checklist on the assignment in Second Draft to make the time after work go faster.

**Why I can't make the changes:** Dr. Weiss's AI policy for English 110 only lets me help you plan, reply to comments and ask her questions. She also wrote in your course thread that AI can't "suggest or write wording" and that "the sentences in the essay have to be yours." Your own rules for me say the same thing. So I haven't touched the draft or added any suggestions, not even grammar fixes. Grammar suggestions are allowed in History 205, but not in this class. She did tell you that turning comments into a checklist is fine, so that's what I did.

**The big issue first:** the draft is about 400 words, which was the length for peer review. The final essay should be about 1,000 words. You'll need to add a lot, not just polish.

**Checklist, in priority order (it links to all 9 open comments):**
1. **Thesis (paragraph 1):** Replace "This essay will look at both sides…" with what you actually think. As Dr. Weiss pointed out, your conclusion already says it: a one-year free trial on the 14 and 22.
2. **Conclusion (paragraph 5):** Drop "there are good arguments on both sides" so the ending backs up your position instead of stepping away from it.
3. **Answer the cost objection (paragraph 3):** You name the cost problem but don't answer it. Where would the missing fifth of the budget come from? Also, did a council member really say the "respectful" line? If so, say who; if not, cut it.
4. **Riverton numbers (paragraph 2):** How much did ridership go up, and where did you read that?
5. **Length:** Items 3, 4 and 6 are your best places to add the missing ~600 words.
6. **Environment paragraph (paragraph 4):** Connect it to fares (free fares lead to fewer cars). Either develop or cut the last sentence about crowded buses.
7. **Comma splices:** "most people think, a monthly pass" and "respectful, I do not think." Use a period or a semicolon. Your grammar score on Essay 1 was 2 out of 4, so do one last read looking for this mistake.
8. **Reread the whole essay, then submit it yourself before 11:59 PM.**

You'll have about three hours after nine. If you run short, do items 1 to 4 first, since Dr. Weiss wrote those comments. If you want, I can message her for you to ask whether an extension is possible.

detail.text: Thesis (p1): Replace the 'both sides' sentence with your actual position. Your conclusion already has it (the one-year trial on the 14 and 22). Say what the council should do and why, in your own words.
